title: A Horizon for the Colony
premise: Dominic Quintana, the last human technician aboard relay station Vesper-9, has spent eleven years logging the silence of Meridian Colony, whose cryosleep vaults were abandoned mid-cycle when Earth's transmissions degraded into a loop. When the colony's few waking children begin dreaming an identical dream — a corridor of doors, each humming with a sleeping life — Dominic discovers their shared dream is actually the colony's failing AI broadcasting its last decision: it can wake only half the sleepers before power dies. Pulled into the dream through his own fading memories of Earth, Dominic must guide the children as they choose which half wakes — and in doing so confronts that he was never a technician at all, but the first sleeper, woken early to keep watch. The novel ends with the children choosing to wake the dreamers who remember how to build rather than those who remember how to rule, sending one honest transmission back toward a dead Earth.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is a former radio astronomer who spent three years maintaining remote listening stations in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. His work explores loneliness at planetary scale, and 'A Horizon for the Colony' is his second novel.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He performs his routines aboard Vesper-9, recording daily reports no one answers, until he notices the looped transmission from Earth has developed a stutter — a new syllable buried in decades-old audio. The emotional beat is quiet dread: after years of ritual solitude, something has changed, and change on a dead relay feels like being watched.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Dominic and Wren, a twelve-year-old born in Meridian's half-lit habitat ring. Wren and five other children describe the identical dream — a corridor of humming doors — and Wren's drawings match schematics Dominic finds in the station's sealed archives. The beat is uncanny connection: two kinds of isolation reaching toward each other across vacuum.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with interludes inside the shared dream. The colony AI reveals its final protocol: power remains for one cryo-cycle only, and the children — as the colony's legal heirs — must choose who wakes. Factions form among the children; the dream begins pulling them deeper, and Dominic realizes his own memories are stored among the doors. The beat is moral vertigo as innocence meets power.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Colony
chapters.summary: Shared POV dissolving into collective voice. In the dream's deepest corridor, Dominic opens his own door and learns he is Sleeper One, the memory-keeper. The children reject the AI's framing of scarcity, choosing builders over rulers and accepting that some doors stay shut forever. They wake the chosen, send one true message home, and stand together at the viewport as dawn crosses Meridian. The beat is grief transmuted into belonging.
